Gerard Baker, the editor-at-large of The Wall Street Journal, thinks Secretary of State Marco Rubio should break ranks with Donald Trump ― while he still can.

“The future of the Republican Party may hinge on one man’s ability to continue playing an impossible role. With his party in eclipse, Marco Rubio’s star keeps rising,” Baker argued in his latest column, published Monday.

Baker, who served as the Rupert Murdoch-owned newspaper’s editor-in-chief until 2018, explored what he called the “paradox” of Rubio’s political rise, saying he has deftly navigated the challenge of publicly representing Trump’s foreign policy while, at the same time, appearing to distance himself from its most polarizing elements.

Rubio “will doubtless one day make the case ― with some justification ― that his continued participation in this grotesquerie helped avoid worse outcomes,” Baker said.

But the columnist argued it was time for Rubio, whom Trump himself has tipped as a potential heir to his MAGA kingdom, to walk away.

“But we have surely reached a point where the right thing to do — for your party, for your soul — is to have the courage to get out and begin the task of restoring some honor to the country you love,” Baker concluded.

Polling currently shows Rubio enjoying a slender lead over Vice President JD Vance in who voters think should become the GOP’s 2028 presidential nominee.

They lead the rest of the pack by quite some distance.

Possible rivals include outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, former Fox News personality Tucker Carlson, Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

None has launched an official campaign, however.
